what-do-bed-bugs-look-like-on-a-bed-a-me.title: What Do Bed Bugs Look Like on a Bed? A Mesa Homeowner's Inspection Guide
what-do-bed-bugs-look-like-on-a-bed-a-me.content:
Adult bed bugs look like flat, reddish-brown, oval insects about the size of an apple seed (roughly 4–5 mm), and on a bed you will usually spot them, or the evidence they leave, along the mattress seams, piping, tags and headboard. If you live in Mesa and you are checking your own bed right now, look for live bugs, tiny pale eggs, translucent shed skins and small dark specks that smear rust-colored when wiped. Everything below is what we look for when we walk into a Mesa bedroom, and it is the same checklist you can run in about ten minutes with a flashlight. If you confirm a problem, our team handles bed bug treatment in Mesa from inspection through follow-up.

What Do Bed Bugs Look Like on a Bed?

Bed bugs on a bed look like small, flat, rust-brown ovals that hide in folds and seams rather than sitting out on the sheet. Fed bugs are swollen, darker and more elongated. Young bugs are pale, straw-colored and can be as small as a pinhead. Most people never see a bug in daylight because they tuck into tight cracks, so the signs around the bug are often what you notice first.

Across homes from Dobson Ranch to Eastmark, we see the same pattern. The bugs cluster within a few feet of where someone sleeps, and the first clue is almost never a crawling bug. It is a cluster of dark specks on the mattress piping, a faint blood spot on a pillowcase, or a bite pattern that shows up every morning.

How Big Is a Bed Bug at Each Life Stage?

A bed bug goes through five nymph stages before adulthood, and each stage has to feed on blood before it molts. That is why size varies so much, and why a bed can hold bugs that look like completely different insects. The table below is how we describe each stage to Mesa homeowners during an inspection.

StageApproximate sizeWhat it looks like
EggAbout 1 mmPearly white, rice-shaped, glued into seams and crevices
Young nymph1.5–2 mmTranslucent, straw-colored, nearly invisible until fed
Older nymph3–4.5 mmTan to light brown, turns reddish after feeding
Unfed adult4–5 mmFlat, oval, mahogany brown, like an apple seed
Fed adult5–7 mmSwollen, longer, dark red to purplish-brown

Where Do I Look First When I Check My Bed for Bed Bugs?

Start at the mattress seams and work outward, because bed bugs hide closest to the person they feed on. Pull the sheets off, turn on a bright flashlight and work in this order:

  1. Mattress piping and seams, especially the head-end corners, where bugs and dark specks collect.
  2. The tag and the underside of the mattress, including the fabric that covers the box spring.
  3. Headboard joints and bed-frame screw holes, which make perfect tight hiding spots.
  4. Nightstand drawers and the gap between the nightstand and the wall.
  5. Baseboards, outlet covers and the edge of the carpet within a few feet of the bed.

A credit card run gently along the seam is a good trick. It pulls out eggs and shed skins that a flashlight alone misses.

What Do Bed Bug Signs Look Like Besides the Bugs Themselves?

The evidence is often easier to find than the insect. These are the signs we point to most often, and finding two or more of them together is a strong indicator of an active infestation:

  • Dark fecal spots. Tiny black or rust-colored dots, about the size of a pen tip, that bleed into the fabric when dampened.
  • Blood smears. Small reddish stains on sheets or pillowcases where a fed bug was crushed.
  • Shed skins. Hollow, translucent, tan shells left behind each time a nymph molts.
  • Eggs and egg shells. Clusters of tiny white specks stuck in seams.
  • A sweet, musty odor. In heavier infestations, some people notice it when they open a closet or pull back bedding.

What Do Bed Bug Bites Look Like?

Bed bug bites are small, red, itchy welts that often show up in lines or clusters on skin exposed while sleeping, such as the arms, neck, face and shoulders. Reactions vary a lot, and some people show no reaction at all. Because mosquito, flea and spider bites can look nearly identical, a bite pattern alone can never confirm bed bugs. You need to find the bug or its signs.

That matters in Mesa, where people sometimes blame bites on mosquitoes after a monsoon. If the bites appear only after sleeping, and never while you are outside in the evening, check the bed before you buy more repellent. If mosquitoes really are the issue, our mosquito control service in Mesa and this guide to stopping mosquitoes in the 85208 area cover that side.

How Do Bed Bugs Get Into Mesa Homes?

Bed bugs are hitchhikers, not a sign of a dirty home. They travel in luggage, backpacks, used furniture and clothing, then settle in wherever people sleep. Mesa has more of that traffic than most people realize, which is why we treat it as a local risk instead of a rare one.

  • Travel and visitors. Phoenix-Mesa Gateway Airport, spring training crowds around Sloan Park and winter visitors all bring luggage through neighborhoods across 85201–85210.
  • Multi-unit housing. Apartments and rentals near downtown Mesa, Mesa Community College and the Superstition Springs area share walls, which lets bugs move between units.
  • Used furniture. Secondhand couches, mattresses and headboards are a classic way to bring a hidden population home.
  • College and shared living. Students and roommates moving in and out move bedding and boxes with them.

Heat does not protect a Mesa home. Bed bugs live indoors at a steady temperature, so a 110°F July does not slow them down the way it slows outdoor pests. If you want the treatment side of the story, our Mesa neighborhood guide to bed bug treatment around Red Mountain walks through what happens after a confirmed find.

Is It Bed Bugs or Something Else?

Several common Arizona household insects get mistaken for bed bugs. Telling them apart saves you from treating the wrong problem. Here is how we sort them out:

Look-alikeHow it differs from a bed bug
Carpet beetle larvaeFuzzy and bristly, often found near wool and closets, and they do not bite
Cockroach nymphsFaster, with longer legs and antennae, and they run when the light comes on
FleasJump, are much smaller, and bites concentrate on ankles and lower legs
Spider beetlesRound and shiny with long legs, usually near stored food
TicksEight legs instead of six, and usually linked to pets

If what you found runs fast and hides behind appliances, see our guide to getting rid of cockroaches in Mesa. If it is a tiny web builder hiding in corners, our Mesa spider guide is a better fit.

What Should I Do If I Find Bed Bugs?

Stay calm, contain the problem and get a professional inspection. Bed bugs spread fastest when people panic and start moving things around. We suggest the following:

  1. Wash and dry bedding on high heat, then bag it until treatment is finished.
  2. Vacuum seams, baseboards and the bed frame, then empty the vacuum outside into a sealed bag.
  3. Do not move items into other rooms or bring in sprays from the store. Over-the-counter products often scatter bugs to new rooms.
  4. Do not toss your mattress until we have inspected. Moving it uncovered can spread bugs through the hallway and into other rooms.
  5. Call us so a technician can confirm the species, find every harborage and build a plan for your home.

We are locally owned and Apache Junction based, have served Arizona families since 2013, and are an AZ ROC licensed team. You can call us in Mesa at (480) 422-8388 or request service online. If a neighbor, apartment or relative is also dealing with bed bugs, tell us. It changes how we plan the job.

Do Bed Bugs Show Up in Nearby Cities Too?

Yes, and we see the same signs throughout the East Valley. We service Gilbert, Chandler, Tempe, Queen Creek, Apache Junction and Gold Canyon, and the inspection steps above apply to all of them. Our neighbors in Gilbert can read our Gilbert 85295 bed bug guide and see our bed bug treatment in Gilbert page, and Queen Creek residents can check the Cortina bed bug guide. For the full list of pest services we offer across town, visit our Mesa pest and termite control overview or the main Mesa services hub.

See how our crew works on our YouTube channel, where we post what a typical service visit looks like.

Frequently Asked Questions About What Bed Bugs Look Like

What do bed bugs look like to the naked eye?

Adult bed bugs are flat, oval and reddish-brown, about the size of an apple seed, and visible without a magnifier. Young bugs are much smaller and pale, so a flashlight and a close look at seams help.

Can you see bed bugs during the day?

Usually not. Bed bugs hide in seams and cracks during the day and come out mostly at night to feed, so finding dark specks, shed skins or eggs is often easier than spotting a live bug.

What do bed bug eggs look like?

Bed bug eggs are about 1 mm long, pearly white and shaped like a tiny grain of rice. They are usually stuck in clusters along mattress seams, headboard joints and other tight crevices.

What do bed bugs look like after they feed?

After feeding, a bed bug becomes swollen, longer and noticeably darker, often dark red to purplish-brown. A recently fed bug also moves more slowly than a hungry one.

Do bed bugs only live in beds?

No. Beds are the most common spot, but bugs also hide in couches, recliners, baseboards, outlet covers and behind picture frames, especially in heavier infestations.

Are bed bugs a sign that my Mesa home is dirty?

No. Bed bugs travel on luggage, clothing and secondhand furniture, and they show up in clean homes, hotels and apartments alike. Cleanliness does not cause them.

how-to-get-rid-of-fruit-mosquitoes-a-mes.title: How to Get Rid of Fruit Mosquitoes: A Mesa Homeowner's Guide to Fruit Flies and Gnats
how-to-get-rid-of-fruit-mosquitoes-a-mes.content:
The tiny "mosquitoes" hovering over your fruit bowl are almost never mosquitoes. They are fruit flies, and you get rid of them by removing whatever they breed in (ripe fruit, a wet drain, a damp trash can), then trapping the adults that are left. If you live in Mesa and the cloud is thick around the kitchen, start with the checklist below, and if the problem is actually biting mosquitoes outside, our team handles mosquito control in Mesa. You can also call us at (480) 422-8388.

How Do You Get Rid of Fruit Mosquitoes?

You get rid of fruit "mosquitoes" in three steps: find and remove the breeding material, clean the drains and bins where eggs hide, and trap the adults until the last ones disappear. Traps alone never finish the job, because a single overlooked banana or slow drain keeps producing a new generation every week or so.

Here is the order we recommend to Mesa homeowners, from Dobson Ranch to Eastmark:

  1. Clear the food source. Throw out overripe fruit, refrigerate produce, and check the pantry for a forgotten potato, onion or bottle of juice.
  2. Empty and wash the trash and recycling. Sticky residue in the bottom of a bin is a perfect nursery.
  3. Clean the drains. Scrub the inside of kitchen and bathroom drains with a stiff brush, because the film on the pipe wall is what drain flies feed on.
  4. Set a simple trap. A small jar with a little apple cider vinegar, a drop of dish soap and a paper funnel catches adults overnight.
  5. Repeat for a week. Eggs you missed will hatch, so keep traps out and sources clean for at least seven to ten days.

Are Fruit Mosquitoes Really Mosquitoes?

No. People search "fruit mosquitoes" for the small flying insects that swarm ripe fruit, but they are usually fruit flies (Drosophila), and sometimes fungus gnats or drain flies. True mosquitoes bite, need standing water to breed, and are mostly a patio and yard problem, not a kitchen one.

The confusion is understandable. All of these insects are small, dark and annoying, and they tend to show up together in summer. The quickest way to tell them apart is to look at where they gather and how they fly.

Fruit Fly vs. Drain Fly vs. Fungus Gnat vs. Mosquito

InsectWhat it looks likeWhere you find itWhat it breeds inBites?
Fruit flyTan to brown, red eyes, about the size of a pinheadFruit bowl, trash can, recycling, sinkRipe or rotting produce, sticky residueNo
Drain flyFuzzy, moth-like, grey wings held like a tentBathroom and kitchen drains, shower wallsSlime film inside slow drainsNo
Fungus gnatSlim, dark, long legs, weak flyerHouseplants, near windowsConstantly wet potting soilNo
MosquitoLong legs, slender body, long mouthpartsPatio, yard, shaded walls, bedrooms at nightStanding water that sits for daysYes

If the insects are in the kitchen and never bite, treat it as a sanitation problem. If you are getting bitten, read our Mesa guide to stopping mosquitoes instead.

Why Do Fruit Flies Show Up So Fast in Mesa Homes?

Mesa's heat speeds up everything a fruit fly needs. Produce ripens faster on the counter, trash warms up quickly in the garage, and a female can lay hundreds of eggs that hatch within a day or two. One forgotten peach can turn into a swarm in days.

Across the 85201 through 85210 ZIP codes, we see the same handful of triggers, and several are specific to the valley:

  • Backyard citrus and fruit trees. Fallen oranges, lemons and grapefruit that bake on the ground ferment quickly and draw flies right to your back door.
  • Garage trash and recycling bins. Bins that sit in the heat develop a sour film that flies love, and the smell travels through the garage door.
  • Monsoon humidity. When the humidity jumps in July through September, damp sink traps, wet sponges and overwatered houseplants hold moisture longer.
  • Disposal and dishwasher gunk. Food residue under the disposal flange is one of the most common hidden breeding spots we find.
  • Wine, beer and juice bottles. A recycling bin of unrinsed bottles is an open invitation, especially near the Fiesta District and other busy households.

What Is the Fastest Way to Kill Fruit Flies in the House?

The fastest safe method is a vinegar trap plus removing the breeding source the same day. The trap kills the adults you can see within hours, while cleaning the source stops the next wave. A fly swatter or spray only kills what is flying right now.

How Do You Make a Fruit Fly Trap?

Pour about an inch of apple cider vinegar into a jar, add a drop of dish soap so the flies sink instead of landing on the surface, and cover the top with plastic wrap poked with small holes, or a rolled paper cone. Set one near the fruit bowl and another near the kitchen sink.

Does Bleach or Boiling Water Clear Drain Flies?

Bleach and boiling water rarely solve it because they run straight past the film on the pipe wall. A stiff brush, a bit of baking soda and hot tap water, or an enzyme drain cleaner from the store, reaches the slime where the larvae live. Do this nightly for a week.

A quick test helps you confirm a drain is the source: tape a piece of clear plastic wrap over the drain opening overnight. If small flies are stuck to the underside in the morning, you have found the nursery.

How Long Do Fruit Flies Take to Go Away?

Once the breeding source is gone, most infestations fade in one to two weeks. The life cycle in warm Arizona kitchens can be as short as a week from egg to adult, so eggs and larvae you missed keep hatching for several days. If flies are still there after two weeks, there is a source you have not found.

Hidden Breeding Spots People Miss

  • The rubber gasket inside the dishwasher door
  • Under the refrigerator drip tray
  • The bottom of the garbage disposal and its rubber splash guard
  • Mop heads and dish rags that stay damp
  • Pet food dishes and water bowls left out overnight
  • Overflow drains in bathroom sinks and floor drains in the garage or laundry room
  • Compost buckets and worm bins kept indoors

When Is It Not Fruit Flies but Real Mosquitoes?

If you are getting bitten, especially around ankles, in the evening or overnight, you are dealing with mosquitoes, not fruit flies. Mosquitoes breed in standing water that sits for more than a few days, and in Mesa that usually means a neglected pool, a clogged gutter, a plant saucer or an irrigation low spot.

In the monsoon months we get the most calls about this. After a storm, water collects in unexpected places, and it only takes a bottle cap of water to get a start. Our neighbors in Gilbert and Chandler deal with the same thing, and we cover the pattern in our Morrison Ranch monsoon guide and the Cooper Commons version.

Where Do Mosquitoes Breed Around a Mesa Yard?

  • Pool covers that collect rainwater
  • Plant saucers and decorative pots
  • Clogged rain gutters and downspout extenders
  • Birdbaths and pet bowls that are not refreshed
  • Low spots where irrigation water pools
  • Drip-line leaks and overflowing evaporative cooler pans

Mosquitoes hide in shaded, humid spots during the day, such as dense shrubs, patio corners and under eaves. Our technicians check those areas first when they visit a property near Red Mountain or Val Vista.

What Can a Pest Control Company Do About Fruit Flies?

A pro inspection finds the source you cannot see, which is the hard part. We look in drains, under appliances, in garage bins and around outdoor fruit trees, and we tell you exactly what is feeding the flies. Sanitation does most of the work, and we are straightforward about that.

What we do not do is pretend a spray fixes a dirty drain. If the flies are in the kitchen, we will show you the source, tell you what to clean, and follow up if it is part of a bigger pest issue. If the real trouble is biting mosquitoes outside or another pest entirely, we handle that too. Our Mesa pest control services cover the full list, and you can request service online any time.

Is It Bed Bugs, Not Flies?

Occasionally. If you are finding bites and no flying insects, the cause may be something else entirely. Our guide on what bed bugs look like on a bed walks through the signs, and our Mesa bed bug treatment page explains what happens next. Roaches can also show up around kitchen drains, which we cover in our Lehi district roach guide.

A Seasonal Checklist for Mesa Kitchens

SeasonWhat to watch forWhat to do
Spring (March to May)Citrus and fruit-tree drop, warming garagesPick up fallen fruit weekly and wash bins monthly
Early summer (June)Heat speeds ripening and trash odorRefrigerate produce and take trash out more often
Monsoon (July to September)Humidity, damp drains, standing water after stormsScrub drains, dump standing water, check plant saucers
Fall (October to November)Holiday produce, cider and bottlesRinse recycling and do not leave fruit out overnight
Winter (December to February)Fewer problems, indoor plants stay wetLet houseplant soil dry between watering

Which Nearby Cities Do We Serve?

We are based in Apache Junction and serve Mesa along with Gilbert, Chandler, Tempe, Queen Creek and Gold Canyon. The same flying-insect questions come up across the East Valley, and we have local write-ups for South Tempe and Sossaman Farms in Queen Creek. You can start at our Mesa page to see everything we offer in town.

Bucksworth Home Services has been locally owned since 2013 by Jordan and Taylor Moore, and our technicians are the ones who answer questions like these every week. You can see how we work on our YouTube channel.

Frequently Asked Questions

How do you get rid of fruit mosquitoes fast?

Remove overripe fruit, wash trash and recycling bins, scrub the drains, and set a vinegar-and-dish-soap trap. The trap catches adults within hours, and cleaning the source keeps new ones from hatching.

Why do I have tiny mosquito-like bugs in my kitchen?

They are most likely fruit flies, drain flies or fungus gnats. They are attracted to ripe produce, slime in drains and wet potting soil, and they do not bite.

Do fruit flies come from nowhere?

No. Adults arrive on produce from the store or drift in from outside, and eggs on fruit skin hatch quickly in warm kitchens. A small number can become a swarm within days.

Will apple cider vinegar really work on fruit flies?

Yes for catching adults. Fermenting vinegar attracts them, and dish soap breaks the surface tension so they cannot escape. It will not stop breeding, so pair it with cleaning.

When should I call a pest control company?

Call if the flies persist after two weeks of cleaning, if you cannot find the source, or if you are being bitten. Mesa homeowners can reach us at (480) 422-8388.

Are fruit flies dangerous?

They do not bite, but they can carry bacteria from drains and garbage onto food. That is one more reason to deal with the source quickly.

If the flies persist after you clean up, our pest control in Mesa team can inspect for the breeding source.

how-to-get-rid-of-fruit-mosquitoes-a-tuc.title: Drain Flies in Tucson Homes: How to Get Rid of Them for Good
how-to-get-rid-of-fruit-mosquitoes-a-tuc.content:
The tiny gray, moth-shaped flies hanging around your Tucson bathroom or kitchen sink are drain flies, and you get rid of them by cleaning the slime film inside the drain where they breed, not by spraying the flies you can see. Most homes clear in one to two weeks once the film is gone. If the flies keep coming back after that, call us at (520) 284-9930 and our technicians will inspect for the source.

What Are Drain Flies, and Why Are They in My Tucson Home?

Drain flies (also called moth flies or sewer flies) are small, fuzzy, gray-brown insects about 1/8 inch long, with wings held like a tent over the body. They do not bite and they do not carry disease the way a mosquito can, but they are a sure sign that organic gunk is building up somewhere wet. Adults flutter rather than fly, and they usually rest on the wall right next to the drain they came from.

Each female lays dozens of eggs in the film of slime, hair, soap and food residue that coats the inside of a drain or trap. The larvae feed on that film. In warm indoor air the whole cycle can finish in about a week to ten days, which is why a couple of flies in the bathroom can turn into a cloud in a long weekend.

How Do I Know It Is a Drain Fly and Not a Fruit Fly or Gnat?

InsectWhat it looks likeWhere you find itHow it moves
Drain flyFuzzy gray, moth-like wingsBathroom walls, tubs, sinks, floor drainsShort, clumsy flutters
Fruit flyTan body, red eyesFruit bowl, trash, recyclingHovers over food
Fungus gnatSlim, dark, long legsWindows, houseplantsWeak, erratic flight
MosquitoLong legs, needle mouthPatios, bedrooms at nightStraight flight, bites

How Can I Find Which Drain the Flies Are Coming From?

Do the tape test: cover the suspect drain overnight with a piece of clear tape or plastic wrap, then check it in the morning. Flies stuck to the underside mean that drain is a breeding site. Test every drain in the area, because the one you notice is often not the one that is producing them.

  1. Dry the area around the drain so the tape sticks.
  2. Tape clear packing tape across the opening, leaving a small gap for air.
  3. Check it the next morning for small gray flies stuck to the sticky side.
  4. Repeat on bathroom sinks, tub drains, shower drains, the laundry standpipe, the kitchen sink and any floor drain in the garage.

Which Drains Do We See Most Often in Tucson?

  • Guest bathrooms and casita baths. A tub or sink that is used a few times a month never gets flushed, and the film dries into a perfect larval bed.
  • Garage and laundry floor drains. Traps dry out in Tucson heat, then get wet again after a monsoon storm.
  • Kitchen sink overflow holes. The slot behind the faucet collects food film that never sees a brush.
  • Older homes near Sam Hughes, Armory Park and the 85705 and 85719 neighborhoods. Older cast iron lines build more rough film than newer plastic pipe.
  • Rarely used showers in snowbird homes. A home that sits closed for months is a common call for us in Oro Valley and Green Valley.

How Do You Get Rid of Drain Flies for Good?

Scrub the pipe wall with a stiff brush, then treat the drain with an enzyme or bio-based drain cleaner that digests the film. Repeat nightly for a week. Killing adults without removing the film only gives you a short break, because the next batch is already growing in the slime.

What Is the Step-by-Step Drain Cleaning Routine?

  1. Remove the stopper or strainer and pull out hair and debris by hand.
  2. Scrub the inside of the drain opening and the overflow slot with a long, stiff bottle brush.
  3. Pour in an enzyme drain cleaner as directed on the label, and let it sit overnight.
  4. Flush with hot tap water in the morning.
  5. Repeat every night for 7 days, and run water in unused drains weekly after that.

Does Bleach, Boiling Water or Vinegar Work on Drain Flies?

Mostly no. Bleach and hot water run straight down the pipe and skip the sticky film clinging to the walls. They may kill a few larvae, but the film stays. A brush plus an enzyme cleaner is the combination that has worked best in the homes we visit.

Why Do Drain Flies Get Worse During Tucson's Monsoon?

Monsoon humidity (roughly July through September) keeps drain film damp and lets eggs survive in traps and floor drains that normally dry out. Storms can also push moisture and organic debris into outdoor drains, so adults find their way into garages and then into the house.

SeasonWhat happens in TucsonWhat to do
SpringWarm up speeds breeding in lightly used drainsRun water in guest bath and casita drains weekly
Early summerHeat dries traps in garage and laundry drainsPour a cup of water into floor drains monthly
MonsoonHumidity and storm moisture revive breedingBrush and treat drains; check for damp spots near the house
FallLingering warmth, reopened snowbird homesFlush every drain before and after seasonal stays
WinterSlower breeding indoorsKeep up weekly flushing

When Should I Call a Pest Control Company About Drain Flies?

Call us if you have cleaned every drain for two weeks and the flies are still there, if they appear in several rooms at once, or if you cannot find the source. Our technicians inspect the visible drains, the areas around them and the garage and yard, and we work out which insect it is before we treat. We do not offer plumbing work, so if the inspection points to a damaged line, we will tell you that plainly.

A drain fly problem can also be a clue about other pests. Roaches love the same damp spots, so we also check entry points for roach elimination in Tucson, and across the wider Tucson pest and termite services we offer. Our guide to sewer roaches in Tucson explains how drains and roaches travel together, and the roach control guide for central Tucson covers the kitchen side.

Could It Be Spiders, Bed Bugs or Mosquitoes Instead?

If you see lots of webbing near the flies, spiders may be feeding on them; our post on spider control near the University of Arizona explains what we do about that. If something is biting you at night, read the Tucson bed bug guide. Drain flies never bite, so biting insects outdoors after a storm are real mosquitoes, and our mosquito control in Tucson service handles those.

How Do I Keep Drain Flies From Coming Back?

Keep every drain moving and clean. Drain flies come back when a drain sits unused or a film is allowed to rebuild, so prevention is mostly a habit, not a product. Here is the routine we suggest to Tucson homeowners after a problem is solved:

  • Run water for 30 seconds in every guest bath, casita and laundry drain once a week.
  • Brush the kitchen sink overflow slot and strainer every month.
  • Add a cup of water to garage and floor drains so the trap never dries out in summer heat.
  • Clean the shower and tub drain strainers of hair every few weeks.
  • Before a long trip or a snowbird season, flush every drain, then check them again when you return.

None of these steps costs anything but a few minutes, and they stop the film that drain flies need. A home that is traveled in and out of often, like a rental or a winter place, benefits the most.

Which Nearby Cities Do We Serve?

Our Tucson branch serves the whole metro, including Oro Valley, Marana, Vail, Catalina Foothills, Green Valley, Sahuarita and Valencia West. If you are in Sahuarita, our Sahuarita and Quail Creek guide covers the outdoor side of flying pests.

You can see everything we do in town on our Tucson page, or request service online and we will get back to you. Bucksworth Home Services has been locally owned since 2013 by Jordan and Taylor Moore, and you can see how we work on our YouTube channel.

Frequently Asked Questions

How do you get rid of drain flies fast?

Scrub the inside of the drain with a stiff brush, treat it with an enzyme drain cleaner overnight and repeat for a week. Adults die off within days once the breeding film is gone.

Where do drain flies come from?

They breed in the slime layer inside drains, traps and overflow slots, and sometimes in other damp organic buildup. They are not "from nowhere"; a lightly used or dirty drain is almost always the source.

Do drain flies mean I have a sewer problem?

Not necessarily. Most of the time it is just film in one drain. If the flies come from many drains at once or you smell sewer gas, have a licensed plumber check your line, since that is outside what we do.

Are drain flies harmful?

They do not bite or sting, but they live in unsanitary film and can leave bacteria on surfaces they land on, so they are worth clearing quickly.

How long do drain flies take to go away?

Plan on seven to fourteen days after you start cleaning. Adults live about two weeks, and new ones stop appearing once the film is gone.

When should I call a pest control company?

Call if the flies persist after two weeks of cleaning, appear in several rooms or you cannot find the source. Tucson homeowners can reach us at (520) 284-9930.

what-do-termites-look-like-a-mesa-homeow.title: What Do Termites Look Like? A Mesa Homeowner's Identification Guide
what-do-termites-look-like-a-mesa-homeow.content:
Termites are small, soft-bodied insects: workers are pale cream-white and about 1/8 inch long, soldiers have a larger orange-brown head, and swarmers (the winged ones) are dark brown to black with two equal-length, milky wings. If you are seeing winged insects indoors in Mesa, the quickest check is the waist and wings: termites have a thick, straight body and wings of equal length, while flying ants are pinched at the waist. Call us at (480) 422-8388 or read about our termite treatment in Mesa if you are not sure what you found.

What Do Termites Look Like Up Close?

A colony has three kinds of termites, and each one looks different. Most people only ever see one of them, which is why the same insect gets described so many ways. In the Mesa homes we inspect, the type you find tells us a lot about where the colony is and what stage it is in.

What Does a Worker Termite Look Like?

Workers are the ones that do the damage, and they stay hidden. They are creamy white to pale tan, about 1/8 to 1/4 inch long, with no wings, no obvious waist and a soft, almost translucent body. You usually see them only when a mud tube or a piece of wood is broken open.

What Does a Soldier Termite Look Like?

Soldiers look like workers with a bigger, harder head, usually orange to brown, and jaw-like mandibles. They guard the colony, so they show up at the front when a tube or gallery is opened. They are a good sign you are looking at termites and not ants.

What Does a Swarmer (Winged Termite) Look Like?

Swarmers are the reproductive termites that leave to start new colonies. They are darker, roughly 3/8 to 1/2 inch long, with a thick waist, straight beaded antennae and two pairs of wings of equal size that are longer than the body. The wings drop off quickly, so a small pile of shed wings on a windowsill is often the first thing a homeowner sees.

Termite vs. Flying Ant: What Is the Difference?

FeatureTermite swarmerFlying ant
WaistThick, straight bodyPinched, narrow waist
AntennaeStraight, beadedBent (elbowed)
WingsFour wings, all the same lengthFront wings longer than the back wings
Wing colorMilky, translucentOften clearer, with visible veins
ColorDark brown to blackBlack, brown or reddish
Where you find themNear windows, light fixtures, with shed wingsNear kitchens, trash, outdoor trails

What Do Termites Look Like in Arizona Specifically?

In Mesa, the termites we deal with most are subterranean termites that live in the soil and travel to your house through the ground, plus drywood termites that live inside the wood itself. Both are small and pale, but they leave different evidence. Subterranean termites leave mud tubes; drywood termites leave tiny pellets.

  • Subterranean termites: pencil-width mud tubes on foundation walls, block walls, stucco weep screeds and slab edges.
  • Drywood termites: small, hard, six-sided pellets (frass) that look like coarse sand or coffee grounds, often piled under a window or a piece of trim.
  • Swarmers: winged termites that come out of the ground or the wood, often after a rain and in the warmer months.

We do not make guesses from a description. A technician identifies the species on site, because the treatment is different for each.

Where Do Termites Hide in a Mesa Home?

Termites avoid light and dry air, so you rarely see the insects themselves. You see where they have been: mud tubes, pellets, shed wings and damaged wood. In Mesa we look first at the places where soil, moisture and wood meet.

Where we lookWhat it can show
Foundation and block wallsMud tubes running up from the soil
Garage walls and slab edgesTubes at the base, or hollow-sounding wood trim
Window sills and door framesShed wings, pellets, small blistered spots in paint
Irrigation valves and hose bibsMoisture that draws subterranean termites close to the house
Attic and eave woodPellets from drywood termites
Wood fences, sheds and patio postsEarly signs in untreated wood touching the ground

Which Mesa Neighborhoods See This Most?

Older homes in Downtown Mesa (85201 and 85210) and established areas like Alta Mesa (85204) and Dobson Ranch (85202) give termites decades of time to find a way in. Newer master-planned areas like Eastmark (85212) are not exempt, since soil disturbed during construction and irrigation can bring termites close to the slab. Homes near the desert preserve in Las Sendas (85207) and Red Mountain also see plenty of activity from all kinds of pests, so we keep termite checks on the list during every visit.

How Do I Tell If It Is Termites or Something Else?

Start with the evidence, not the insect. A few clues separate termites from the look-alikes people confuse them with.

  • Mud tubes vs. dirt trails: termite tubes are enclosed and stay attached when brushed; ant trails are open and scatter.
  • Pellets vs. dust: drywood termite pellets are uniform and six-sided; wood dust from other insects is fine and powdery.
  • Hollow wood: tap a suspect board with a screwdriver handle. A papery, hollow sound is a reason to call.
  • Winged insects at a window: use the waist, antennae and wing test from the table above.

What Should I Photograph for a Technician?

  1. Place a coin next to the insect, tube or pellets so we can see the size.
  2. Take one wide photo of the area and one close-up with the flash on.
  3. Save a few of the insects in a sealed bag or a piece of clear tape if you can.
  4. Do not spray them. Spraying scatters the colony and makes the inspection harder.

What Should I Do If I Think I Found Termites?

Stop, take photos and book an inspection. Do not disturb the tubes or treat the area yourself; a store-bought spray usually drives termites a few feet and leaves the colony alive. Our technicians check the whole structure, identify the species and explain what we find in plain terms, with no pressure.

Our signs of termites guide for Mesa homes covers the damage side of this, and our overview of pest control in Mesa lists everything else we treat. If the winged insects turn out to be ants, our ant control in Mesa service and the Mesa ant elimination guide are the right place to start.

When Are You Most Likely to See Termites in Mesa?

You are most likely to see termites after rain or irrigation soaks the ground, because that is when swarmers tend to come out. In Mesa that often means the summer monsoon, but a leaking hose bib or a heavily watered planting bed can set off activity at any time of year. Workers stay active underground all year, which is why we recommend an inspection no matter the season.

Time of yearWhat homeowners tend to noticeWhat to do
SpringNew mud tubes after warm days, softened wood near irrigationWalk the foundation and check hose bibs
Summer monsoonWinged swarmers at windows and lights after stormsSave a few insects and shed wings for ID
FallPiles of pellets, or tubes revealed while cleaning out garagesPhotograph with a coin for scale
WinterQuiet, but damage keeps going out of sightGood time to schedule a full inspection

None of this replaces an inspection. A termite problem can run for a long time before anything shows up inside, so the earlier a technician looks, the more options you have.

Do Termites Look the Same in Nearby Cities?

Yes, the insect looks the same across the Valley; what changes is the soil, the age of the homes and how close they sit to desert. We also work in Gilbert, Chandler, Queen Creek, San Tan Valley and Apache Junction. These local guides cover termite treatment near you:

  • Termite treatment in Gilbert, plus our guide to the best termite company in Gilbert
  • Expert termite treatment for Chandler homes
  • Termite company guide for Apache Junction, where we are based, and our pest control in Apache Junction page

You can see everything we do on our Mesa page, or request service online. Bucksworth Home Services has been locally owned since 2013 by Jordan and Taylor Moore, and you can watch how we work on our YouTube channel.

Frequently Asked Questions

What do termites look like to the naked eye?

Workers are tiny, creamy-white and soft-bodied, about 1/8 inch long. Swarmers are dark with long, milky wings. Most of the time you see the damage or mud tubes instead of the insect.

What do termite droppings look like?

Drywood termite droppings are small, hard, six-sided pellets about the size of a grain of sand, usually in a little pile under the spot where they were pushed out of the wood.

Do termites look like ants?

They can at a glance, but termites have a thick waist, straight antennae and wings of equal length. Ants have a pinched waist, bent antennae and unequal wings.

What do termite mud tubes look like?

They are narrow, pencil-width tunnels of dirt on foundation walls, block walls and slab edges. Termites use them to travel from the soil to wood without drying out.

Are termites visible in the daytime?

Rarely. Workers and soldiers stay hidden inside wood, soil and tubes. Swarmers are the exception and can appear at windows and lights.

Who do I call if I find termites in Mesa?

Call Bucksworth at (480) 422-8388 and send us photos. We will inspect, identify the species and explain the options.
what-do-termites-look-like-a-mesa-homeow.excerpt: Termites are small and soft-bodied: workers are creamy white, soldiers have an orange-brown head, and swarmers are dark with equal-length milky wings.

how-to-remove-a-wasp-nest-a-tempe-homeow.title: How to Remove a Wasp Nest: A Tempe Homeowner's Safety-First Guide
how-to-remove-a-wasp-nest-a-tempe-homeow.content:
The safest way to remove a wasp nest in Tempe is to identify the wasp first, treat a small, low, open paper wasp nest at dusk from a distance with a labeled wasp spray, and call a professional for anything high, enclosed, in a wall, or as big as your fist or larger. If anyone in the house is allergic to stings, skip DIY entirely. Call us at (480) 422-8388 or read about our bee and wasp removal in Tempe and we will send a technician.

What Kind of Wasp Nest Do I Have?

Before you remove anything, work out what you are dealing with, because the right method depends on the nest. In the Tempe homes we visit, most nests fall into three groups, and one of them is not a wasp nest at all.

  • Paper wasps: an open, umbrella-shaped comb with visible hexagonal cells, usually hanging from an eave, a patio rafter, a ceiling fan bracket or a block-wall cap. This is the most common nest we see.
  • Mud daubers: small tubes or organ-pipe shapes of dried mud on walls and garage ceilings. They are not aggressive and rarely need treatment.
  • Bees, not wasps: a hive inside a wall, meter box or tree with a steady stream of insects going in and out. Do not spray these. Bees need a different approach, and a hive that has been sprayed can leave honey and comb behind that attract new problems.

How Can I Tell a Wasp From a Bee?

Wasps are slim, smooth and shiny with a narrow waist and long legs that dangle in flight. Bees are rounder, fuzzier and stockier. If you cannot tell from a safe distance, take a photo with your phone zoom and text it to us. We would rather identify it for you than have you guess.

Nest typeWhat it looks likeWhere we find it in TempeDIY realistic?
Paper waspOpen comb, umbrella shape, gray-brownPatio eaves, fascia boards, ramada raftersSometimes, if small and reachable from the ground
Mud dauberDried mud tubesGarage ceilings, block walls, under patio coversYes, scrape off after the insects leave
Yellowjacket or hornet-typeEnclosed paper ball with one entranceWall voids, attic edges, shrubsNo, call a professional
Honey bee hiveWax comb, heavy traffic at one holeWalls, meter boxes, tree cavitiesNo, never spray

How Do I Safely Remove a Small Paper Wasp Nest Myself?

If the nest is smaller than your palm, in the open, and reachable from the ground, many homeowners handle it themselves. Do it in the evening or just before sunrise, when the whole colony is on the nest and wasps are slow and calm. Midday heat in Tempe makes the colony active and defensive, and this is when most stings happen.

What Do I Need Before I Start?

  • A wasp-and-hornet spray labeled for nests that shoots a stream of 10 to 20 feet
  • Long sleeves, long pants, closed shoes, gloves and eye protection
  • A flashlight with a red lens or cover, since wasps are less drawn to red light
  • A clear exit path, with the door open behind you and pets and kids inside

What Are the Steps?

  1. Stand at the longest range the spray allows and aim at the nest opening, not the wasps in the air.
  2. Soak the nest for several seconds, then back away immediately. Do not stay to watch.
  3. Wait a full day, then check from a distance. If wasps still come and go, repeat the treatment that evening.
  4. Once it is quiet for 24 hours, knock the nest down with a long pole or scrape it off and bag it.
  5. Spray or wash the attachment spot so scent marks fade and a new queen is less likely to rebuild there.

Never use a ladder for a nest above your head. Most serious wasp injuries we hear about are falls, not stings.

When Should I Call a Professional Instead?

Call us when the nest is higher than you can reach safely from the ground, bigger than your hand, enclosed in a wall or soffit, in the ground, or when someone in your home has ever had a bad reaction to a sting. A wasp nest in an attic vent or block-wall void is also a job for a professional, because the wasps you see outside are only a fraction of the colony inside.

Here is how the two routes compare for a typical Tempe home.

SituationDIYProfessional
Small open nest under a low patio eaveReasonable with protective clothing and dusk timingFast and safe, one visit
Nest above a second-story windowNot recommendedRecommended
Nest inside a wall, soffit or attic ventNot recommendedRequired
Family member with sting allergyDo not attemptRequired
Wasps returning after you treatedStop and reassessRecommended

What Should I Do If I Get Stung?

Move away from the nest, wash the sting with soap and water, and apply a cold pack. Wasps can sting more than once, so leave the area fully. Call 911 right away for trouble breathing, swelling of the face or throat, dizziness, or hives spreading across the body. Multiple stings at once also deserve medical attention even without an allergy.

Why Are Wasps So Common in Tempe Yards?

Tempe has what wasps want: water, shelter and food. Around Tempe Town Lake and The Lakes (85282), irrigation, ponds and patio misters give paper wasps a reliable water source through the dry months. South Tempe (85284) has mature trees, block walls and covered patios that offer sheltered spots to build. Near the ASU campus area (85281), older rentals and shared patios often have eaves nobody checks for months, so a nest can grow all season before someone notices.

Papago Park and the Hayden Butte area (85281) bring desert plants and open rock that support a steady wasp population right next to neighborhoods. In Tempe Royal Palms (85283), older homes have more eaves, vents and gaps for queens to scout. None of this means you did something wrong. It means the first spring queen found a good spot.

When Is Wasp Season in Tempe?

Queens wake up as the weather warms and start small nests in spring. By midsummer a nest can hold a large colony, and activity often stays high into the fall as long as nights stay mild. We keep treating wasps well into October, so a late-season nest is still worth dealing with.

Time of yearWhat is happeningWhat to do
Early springQueens start small nestsCheck eaves and knock down tiny nests early
Late spring to summerColony grows fast, workers defend aggressivelyTreat at dusk, or call us for larger nests
Monsoon seasonHumidity and storms push wasps into sheltered spotsInspect patios, garages and attic vents
FallColonies still active, last nests builtTreat and seal entry points before winter

How Do I Keep Wasps From Coming Back?

Removing the nest is only half the job. Without prevention, a new queen often rebuilds in the same protected spot the next season. We walk the property with homeowners and suggest steps that work for Tempe lots.

  • Check eaves, patio covers, ceiling fans and gas meter boxes every few weeks in spring and summer.
  • Seal gaps in fascia, soffit vents and block-wall caps with screen or sealant.
  • Fix dripping hose bibs and irrigation leaks that give wasps water.
  • Keep trash and pet food covered, since wasps also scavenge protein.
  • Have us treat the attachment spots after removal so the area is less attractive.

A wasp problem often shows up alongside other pests. Water features that draw wasps also bring mosquitoes, and we cover that in our guide to monsoon mosquitoes in Tempe. Rock and block-wall cavities that shelter wasps can also hold bark scorpions, which is why our Tempe scorpion prevention guide is worth a read.

What Do Our Technicians Do During a Wasp Visit?

When you call, we ask where the nest is, how big it is and whether anyone is allergic. A technician arrives in protective gear, confirms the species and treats the nest. We remove it when it is safe to do so and treat the attachment point. We do not sell you a bigger job than you have. A single paper wasp nest is a single visit, and if we find a hidden colony in a wall we will tell you exactly what that involves before we start.

If the wasps are only part of a broader problem, our pest control in Tempe page lists everything we handle, and the main Tempe service page shows all of our work in the city.

Do You Also Treat Wasps Near Tempe?

Yes. Tempe borders several cities we serve every day, and the wasp question comes up in all of them. Neighbors in the East Valley can read about bee and wasp removal in Mesa, bee and wasp removal in Chandler and bee and wasp removal in Gilbert. We also serve Ahwatukee and Scottsdale.

If you want to compare how nests behave in neighboring areas, these local write-ups cover other parts of the East Valley:

  • Wasp nest removal in Chandler near Cooper Commons
  • Gilbert bee and wasp removal guide for Agritopia
  • Professional bee removal in Mesa for the 85208 area

Ready to book? Request service online or call (480) 422-8388. Bucksworth Home Services has been locally owned since 2013 by Jordan and Taylor Moore, and you can see how we work on our YouTube channel.

Frequently Asked Questions

How do I get rid of a wasp nest by myself?

For a small, open nest within reach, spray a labeled wasp-and-hornet product at dusk from the maximum distance, then back away and check the next day. Remove the nest only after activity stops. Do not use a ladder or try this if you are allergic.

What is the best time of day to remove a wasp nest?

Late evening or just before sunrise. The whole colony is on the nest, the wasps are calmer and fewer are out foraging.

Will a wasp nest go away on its own?

Paper wasp colonies die off after the season, but the nest stays until it is removed, and the colony can sting in the meantime. Queens may also rebuild nearby the next year.

Is it dangerous to knock down a nest with water or a broom?

Yes. Knocking down an active nest disturbs the whole colony and is a common way people get stung several times. Treat the nest first and remove it only when it is quiet.

How do I know if the nest is a wasp or a bee hive?

Wasps have slim, smooth bodies and build papery nests. Bees are fuzzier and rounder and usually nest in cavities with wax comb. If you are unsure, send us a photo before you spray.

Who do I call for wasp removal in Tempe?

Call Bucksworth at (480) 422-8388. Tell us where the nest is and whether anyone is allergic, and we will schedule a technician.

how-long-can-mosquitoes-live-a-chandler-.title: How Long Can Mosquitoes Live? A Chandler Homeowner's Guide to Mosquito Lifespans
how-long-can-mosquitoes-live-a-chandler-.content:
Most adult mosquitoes live about one to four weeks, and in Chandler's warm months the common backyard species usually sit near the short end of that range. Males live around a week, females typically two to four weeks, and some overwintering house mosquitoes can last for months. The adults you see are only the visible part, though: the next generation can be hatching in a flowerpot saucer right now. If you are tired of waiting them out, call us at (480) 422-8388 or read about our mosquito control in Chandler.

How Long Can a Mosquito Live in Arizona?

The honest answer is that it depends on the species, the sex of the mosquito, and the weather. In the Chandler yards we treat, two kinds of mosquito do most of the biting, and they live a little differently.

  • Aedes aegypti (the yellow fever mosquito): a small, black-and-white striped day-biter that breeds in tiny containers of water. Adult females commonly live two to four weeks in warm weather.
  • Culex (the southern house mosquito): a brownish evening and night biter that breeds in stagnant, dirty water such as neglected pools, clogged drains and retention areas. Females can live several weeks, and mated females can overwinter in sheltered spots and survive for months.
  • Males of both species: they do not bite, feed on plant nectar and usually live about a week.

Why Do Some Mosquitoes Seem to Last Forever?

They do not. What feels like one immortal mosquito is a steady stream of new ones. A single female can lay eggs several times in her life, and each batch can contain dozens to over a hundred eggs. If there is standing water within flight range, you get replacements faster than the older ones die off.

How Long Does the Whole Mosquito Life Cycle Take?

In summer heat the aquatic stages move quickly. Under typical warm conditions a mosquito can go from egg to flying adult in roughly a week to ten days, which is why a puddle that fills after a monsoon storm can turn into a swarm before the following weekend.

StageWhere it livesTypical length in warm weatherWhat it means for your yard
EggOn or just above the waterline of a container; Aedes eggs can survive dry spells1 to 3 days to hatch once wet; Aedes eggs can wait months for waterDry containers can still hold eggs. Scrub, do not just tip
Larva ("wrigglers")Standing waterAbout 4 to 7 daysVisible as small wiggling specks near the surface
PupaStanding water1 to 3 daysTumbling, comma-shaped; adult emerges next
AdultShaded plants, block walls, patiosMales about a week; females 2 to 4 weeks or moreThis is the stage that bites and the one sprays and barrier treatments target

Why Are Mosquitoes Worse in Chandler After Monsoon Storms?

Chandler is dry most of the year, so mosquitoes here depend on the water people create or the water the monsoon leaves behind. Late June through September, afternoon storms fill low spots, saucers, tarps, buckets and the corners of flat roofs. Humidity also helps adults survive longer between blood meals, so the same mosquito can last closer to the top of its range than it would in dry May air.

Irrigation matters just as much. In south Chandler neighborhoods like Ocotillo and Sun Groves, lakes, water features and green belts give adults cool, shaded resting spots and give larvae places to grow. In older areas like Downtown Chandler (85225) and Andersen Springs (85224 and 85226), mature trees, planter pots and clogged yard drains do the same job on a smaller scale.

Which Chandler Spots Do We Find Standing Water Most Often?

  • Plant saucers and decorative pots on patios and entries
  • Pool covers, pool equipment pads and neglected or green pools
  • Clogged yard drains, French drains and low spots near block walls
  • Bird baths, pet bowls and kids' toys left outside
  • Irrigation boxes with a cracked lid and a leaking valve
  • Flat-roof and gutter corners that hold a film of water

Can You Wait Out Mosquitoes Instead of Treating?

Not realistically. Because each adult lives a few weeks and keeps laying eggs, waiting only works if you also remove the water. If you take away the breeding spots and nothing is breeding on neighboring lots, the population fades in about a month. In a typical Chandler subdivision, though, a neighbor's pool, a retention basin or an irrigation leak a few houses away keeps feeding yours.

That is why we pair two things: cutting off the breeding sites you can reach, and treating the places adults rest so the ones already there do not keep biting while the cycle catches up.

What Actually Works to Reduce Mosquitoes at Home?

Here is the order we recommend to homeowners, from simplest to most involved.

  1. Dump and scrub weekly. Empty every container that holds water, and scrub the sides, because Aedes eggs stick to the wall just above the waterline.
  2. Fix the slow leaks. A weeping hose bib or a broken irrigation valve box can make a permanent puddle.
  3. Keep pools circulating and covered properly. A pool that is running and balanced does not breed mosquitoes. A green one will.
  4. Trim dense, shaded plants against walls. Adults rest in cool shade during the day. Opening up the vegetation takes away daytime hiding places.
  5. Use a fan on the patio. Mosquitoes are weak fliers, and a steady fan makes it hard for them to reach you.
  6. Bring in a professional for the resting areas. A technician treats the shaded foliage, block-wall bases and under-patio areas where adults rest, and checks for breeding sites you may have missed.

What About Candles, Bug Zappers and Sprays From the Store?

Citronella candles and zappers have little effect on a yard-wide population, and a zapper kills many harmless insects. Repellent applied to skin is useful for the hours you are outside, but it does not touch the population. They are fine as extras, not as the plan.

Does Mosquito Season in Chandler Ever Really End?

Activity slows with cooler nights, but it rarely stops completely in the Phoenix area. Warm stretches in the fall and a mild winter day can keep some adults flying, and female Culex that settle into garages, block-wall gaps and dense shrubs can wait out the cold and restart in spring. In practice, we see the most pressure from the first warm spring days through the end of the monsoon, with a lingering tail into fall.

Are Mosquitoes in Chandler a Health Concern?

Mostly they are a nuisance, but Culex mosquitoes in the Phoenix area can carry West Nile virus, and Maricopa County runs a public mosquito surveillance and vector control program for that reason. If you or a family member develop a high fever, severe headache or neck stiffness after mosquito bites, contact a doctor. We do not give medical advice, but we can help you shrink the number of mosquitoes around your home.

How Does Mosquito Control in Chandler Differ From Mesa, Gilbert and Tempe?

The biology is the same, but the water sources change. Gilbert's master-planned neighborhoods with community lakes, such as Morrison Ranch, behave differently from Mesa's older irrigated lots around 85208 or south Tempe's block-wall yards. We have written local guides for each, and the lifespan answer above applies in all of them:

  • monsoon mosquito control in Chandler's Cooper Commons and Ocotillo areas
  • monsoon mosquitoes in Gilbert's Morrison Ranch
  • how to stop mosquitoes in Mesa's 85208 area
  • monsoon mosquitoes in south Tempe

We also serve Gilbert, Mesa, Tempe, Queen Creek and Apache Junction, where our headquarters is located.

What Should I Do If Mosquitoes Are Not the Only Pest Around My Chandler Home?

Standing water and dense shade attract more than mosquitoes. If you are also seeing roaches near the patio or scorpions near block walls, our technicians can look at all of it in one visit. See our pest and termite services in Chandler, read about roach control in Ocotillo, or learn how to keep scorpions out of a Chandler home. You can also browse everything we do on our Chandler service page.

When you are ready for a technician, request service online or call us.

Frequently Asked Questions

How long can a mosquito live without feeding?

Adult mosquitoes can often survive several days to a couple of weeks without a blood meal because they also feed on plant nectar. Females need blood to produce eggs, not to stay alive, so a mosquito that has not bitten you recently is not necessarily weak.

How long do mosquito bites last?

Most bites itch for a day or two and the bump fades within a few days. Large swelling, spreading redness or fever deserves a call to a doctor.

How long do mosquitoes live indoors?

Indoors, away from heat and sun, a female can live a few weeks as long as there is nectar, moisture and a place to rest. Most indoor mosquitoes in Chandler get in through gaps around doors and unscreened openings. Fix the screens and check for damp spots.

Do mosquitoes die in Arizona summer heat?

Extreme dry heat shortens adult life, so mosquitoes stay in shaded, cooler, more humid spots during the day. After a monsoon storm they come back out in numbers.

How many times can a mosquito bite in its life?

Each female usually takes a blood meal for every batch of eggs she lays, so over several weeks she may bite several times.

Who do I call for mosquito control in Chandler?

Call Bucksworth at (480) 422-8388, or request service online. Tell us where you see them most, and we will send a technician to your Chandler address.
how-long-can-mosquitoes-live-a-chandler-.excerpt: Most adult mosquitoes live one to four weeks in Chandler's warm months, but each one can lay eggs that hatch in days. Here is how to break the cycle.

do-bumble-bees-sting-a-chandler-homeowne.title: Do Bumble Bees Sting? A Chandler Homeowner's Guide to Bumble Bees, Carpenter Bees and Honey Bees
do-bumble-bees-sting-a-chandler-homeowne.content:
Yes, bumble bees can sting, but only the females, and they sting only when they feel threatened, such as when a nest is disturbed or a bee is pinched or trapped. A bumble bee is much less defensive than a honey bee or a wasp. In Chandler, though, the big, fuzzy "bumble bee" hovering at your eaves is often a carpenter bee, and the bee that actually sends people to urgent care is usually an Africanized honey bee or a paper wasp. If you have bees on your property and you are not sure what they are, call us at (480) 422-8388 or read about our bee and wasp removal in Chandler.

Do Bumble Bees Sting People?

Female bumble bees have a stinger and can use it, and unlike a honey bee, a bumble bee can sting more than once because its stinger is not left behind. Males have no stinger at all. In practice, bumble bees are some of the calmest bees you will meet. They are busy foraging, and they tend to ignore people who ignore them.

The situations where we hear about bumble bee stings are almost always the same: someone reached into a pot or a dense shrub where a small nest was hidden, stepped on a bee in the grass, or swatted at one near the face. A sting from a bumble bee feels like a sharp, burning pinch, and for most people the swelling and soreness fade within a day or two.

Do Bumble Bees Sting More Than Once?

They can. A honey bee's barbed stinger usually stays in the skin, which is why a honey bee generally stings once. A bumble bee's stinger is smoother, so a threatened bumble bee can sting repeatedly. That sounds worse than it is, because a bumble bee has to be pushed pretty hard to get there.

What Does a Bumble Bee Sting Feel Like?

Most people describe it as a hot, sharp sting followed by redness, a raised bump and itching. It is similar to a honey bee sting for the average person. The part that matters is not how it feels but how your body reacts. Anyone who develops hives, swelling of the face or throat, trouble breathing, dizziness or a racing heart after any bee or wasp sting needs emergency care. Call 911. We are a pest company and cannot give medical advice, but that rule is the one to remember.

What Bees Do We Actually See Around Chandler Homes?

Bumble bees do live in Arizona, but in the low desert around Chandler they are far less common than the bees below. Most calls we run on "big fuzzy bees" turn out to be something else. Here is how the common ones compare.

InsectWhat it looks likeWhere you find it in ChandlerWill it sting?
Bumble beeLarge, round, fuzzy, yellow and black on the abdomenFlowering shrubs and gardens; small ground or clump nestsFemales can, rarely; males cannot
Carpenter beeLarge like a bumble bee, but the abdomen is shiny and mostly bareDrilling round holes in fascia boards, pergolas, wood fences and patio beamsMales hover and dive but cannot sting; females seldom sting
Honey bee (including Africanized)Smaller, tan-brown and slim, less fuzzyHives in walls, meter boxes, tree cavities, block-wall gaps and eavesYes, and Africanized colonies defend aggressively in large numbers
Paper waspSlim, long-legged, with an open umbrella-shaped nestEaves, patio covers, light fixtures, under gate framesYes, and they sting repeatedly
Ground-nesting beesSmall, solitary, often dusty lookingBare dirt, rock yard edgesSeldom; they are not defensive

Why Do Carpenter Bees Get Mistaken for Bumble Bees?

Size and sound. Both are chunky and loud. The quickest test is the abdomen: a bumble bee's is fuzzy, while a carpenter bee's is smooth and glossy. If the bee is hovering in front of a wooden beam and you can see a perfectly round half-inch hole with sawdust beneath it, you have carpenter bees, not bumble bees.

How Can I Tell If the Bees at My House Are Dangerous?

Behavior tells you more than appearance. The bees to take seriously are the ones that stay in one place and guard it. Look for these signs.

  • A steady stream of bees entering and leaving one opening, such as a gap in a block wall, a utility box, a wall void or a tree hollow. That is usually a honey bee colony.
  • A low hum from inside a wall or warm, stained stucco and drywall.
  • Bees that follow you or bump into you when you are 20 or more feet from the nest.
  • A gray or tan paper nest with visible cells, which means wasps, not bees.

If you see any of these, do not spray the opening, do not try to seal it and do not swat at the bees. A disturbed colony can turn defensive in seconds, and a sealed wall void with a live hive inside is a bigger problem later, with honey stains and comb that can attract other pests.

Why Are There More Stinging Insects Around Chandler in Spring and Fall?

Chandler's irrigated neighborhoods give bees what the open desert does not: reliable water and flowers. In south Chandler communities like Ocotillo (85248) and Sun Groves (85249), lakes, green belts and flowering landscaping draw foraging bees all season. In established areas such as Andersen Springs (85224 and 85226) and Downtown Chandler (85225), older block walls, mature trees and stucco gaps give honey bees plenty of places to settle.

Swarms are most common in the warm shoulder seasons, when a colony splits and a cluster of bees lands on a tree, a fence post or a wall while scouts look for a cavity. A swarm hanging in a tree is usually calm for a short while, but it is a good moment to call a professional rather than approach it.

Do Bumble Bees Nest in Chandler Yards?

Occasionally. Bumble bees nest in small colonies, often in an abandoned rodent burrow, a pile of leaves or a hollow beneath a pot. A bumble bee nest is far smaller than a honey bee hive, with a few dozen bees at most, and it dies back on its own at the end of the season. If it is not in the way, leaving it alone is the easiest option. If it is next to your front door or a play area, call us and we will tell you honestly what is there and what is worth doing.

What Should I Do If I Get Stung by a Bee?

Move away from the area calmly, because stinging insects can release alarm signals that attract others. Then follow these steps.

  1. Walk away from the nest or the bee. Do not run in circles and do not flail.
  2. Remove a stinger if one is left in the skin. Scrape it out with a fingernail or card. This applies to honey bees, not bumble bees.
  3. Wash the area with soap and water and apply a cold pack.
  4. Watch for a reaction over the next several minutes to hours. Call 911 for trouble breathing, swelling of the face or throat, widespread hives or fainting.
  5. Go indoors and keep children and pets away from the spot until the source is dealt with.

If you were stung more than a handful of times, see a doctor even if you feel fine. We cannot give medical advice, but multiple stings can cause reactions in people who have no known allergy.

Should I Remove Bees From My Chandler Home or Leave Them Alone?

It depends on what they are and where they are. Bees are pollinators, and a few bumble bees in a flowering bush are not a problem. A honey bee colony inside a wall, an eave or a meter box next to your door is a different matter, and it is not a do-it-yourself job in Arizona, where Africanized bees are common.

How Do I Keep Stinging Bees and Wasps Away From My Yard?

  • Seal gaps larger than about a quarter inch around meter boxes, pipe penetrations and block-wall seams, but only after you are sure no bees are inside.
  • Check eaves, patio covers and gate frames every few weeks in spring and fall for the start of a paper wasp nest.
  • Fix irrigation leaks and drips, because bees come to water.
  • Paint or seal exposed wood on pergolas and fascia boards to discourage carpenter bees.
  • Keep trash cans closed and clean up sweet drink spills on the patio.
  • Do not plant dense flowering shrubs right against the doorway if you have an allergy in the family.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do bumble bees sting?

Female bumble bees can sting, and they can sting more than once, but they are not aggressive and usually only sting when handled or when their nest is disturbed. Male bumble bees do not have a stinger.

Do bumble bees die after they sting?

No. Unlike a honey bee, a bumble bee's stinger is not barbed enough to stay in the skin, so it usually survives the sting.

Are carpenter bees dangerous?

Not to people. Males cannot sting and often hover close to you, and females seldom sting. The damage they cause is to unpainted wood, where they drill nesting holes.

How do I know if bees in my wall are honey bees?

Look for a steady stream of small, tan-brown bees going in and out of one opening, and listen for a hum inside the wall. Do not seal the opening. Call a professional to identify and remove the colony.

Are Africanized honey bees in Chandler?

Africanized honey bees are common across the Phoenix area, and any wild colony should be treated as potentially defensive. Keep people and pets away and have the colony handled by a professional.
